diagnostic_evidence.quote: The improved noise dependence to $\frac{n}{m}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\nu}$ can be obtained for free by performing the same estimates above \cite[Eq. (4.5)]{cohen2017optimal} without the last inequality.
By taking $\iid$ samples $\XX$ from a measure $\nu\in\mathcal P(\Omega)$, where $\nu(\d x) = w^{-1}(x)\mu(\d x)$
the error bound in \eqref{oracle-l2} is $\mathcal O(\eta)$ if $m\gtrsim n\max\{\log n, \frac{1}{\eta}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\nu}\}
Thus, \eqref{newb} improves the bound in Theorem \ref{thm:cm17} in terms of sample complexity.

issues.failure_explanation: For the weighted least-squares estimator with Christoffel sampling, the leading-order noise contribution is (1/m) E_nu[w^2 sigma^2 Phi_n] = (n/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_mu}, because w Phi_n = n and dnu = w^{-1} dmu. The stated term (n/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_nu} = (1/m) int sigma^2 Phi_n dmu is a different, generally incomparable quantity (it is the noise level of unweighted mu-sampling). Counterexample: mu uniform on [0,1], V_2 = span{1, sqrt(3)(2x-1)}, so w = 2/Phi_2 and nu = (Phi_2/2)mu; take f = 0 (so OPT = 0) and sigma^2 = c t_eta uniform on [1/2-eta, 1/2+eta]. The true noise variance is exactly (1/m) E_nu[w^2 sigma^2 Phi_2] = 2c/m, while the stated noise term is (2/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_nu} = (c/m)(1+4 eta^2), which is strictly smaller than 2c/m for any eta < 1/2, so the stated bound is violated (by a factor approaching 2). The claimed derivation is also an invalid inference: performing the cited Cohen-Migliorati estimates without the last inequality yields (1/m) E_nu[w^2 sigma^2 Phi_n] = (n/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_mu}, not the L2_nu term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the noise term in Theorem thm:cm17 by (n/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_mu} (equivalently (1/m) E_nu[w^2 sigma^2 Phi_n], which the cited estimate without the last inequality actually yields); update the introduction's complexity formula accordingly; and rederive the comparison in Remark rem:compare via Cauchy-Schwarz, ||sigma sqrt(Phi_n/n)||^2_{L1_mu} <= ||sigma||^2_{L2_mu}, which preserves the improvement claim.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:cm17's guarantee fails whenever ||sigma||^2_{L2_nu} < ||sigma||^2_{L2_mu} (noise mass concentrated where Phi_n < n). The introduction's sample-complexity characterization of plain optimally weighted least squares and the comparison chain in Remark rem:compare are written against this wrong baseline and must be adjusted. The paper's own results (thm:main, thm:conv) are proved independently of this term and remain valid; the hybrid method's superiority also survives the correction because ||sigma sqrt(Phi_n/n)||^2_{L1_mu} <= ||sigma||^2_{L2_mu}.
issues.title: False noise term (n/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_nu} in Theorem thm:cm17; the correct term under Christoffel sampling is (n/m)||sigma||^2_{L2_mu}
issues.why_classification: The stated bound is false, so no forced typo-level correction exists: the repair replaces the noise functional with an incomparable one and requires rederiving the downstream baseline comparison. However, the correction is local, needs no new proof architecture, and leaves all substantive results and the advertised improvement intact, so it is moderate rather than serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, when writing $\bm Y = \E[\bm Y] + (\bm Y-\E[\bm Y])$, the noiseless term conditional on $\XX$, $\E[\bm Y| \XX] = \E[\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm b]$ is not necessarily in $\col(\bm X)$.
the estimator $\widehat{\bm\alpha}(\bm p)$ is unbiased for $\bar{\bm\alpha}$ if $\bm f\in\col(\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V)$

issues.failure_explanation: E[Y|X] = (1/sqrt(m)) (sqrt(w(x_i)) f(x_i))_i lies in col(W^{1/2}V) iff f agrees with SOME element of V_n on the sampled points X. The asserted necessary condition, (f - f*)(x_i) = 0 for all i, and the gloss that this means f in V_n, are both false. Counterexample: V_1 = span{1} on [0,1] with uniform mu, m = 1, and f = v + g with v in V_1, g nonzero and orthogonal to V_1, g(x_1) = 5; then f(x_1) equals the value at x_1 of the constant v + 5 in V_1, so E[Y|X] is in col(X), yet (f - f*)(x_1) = g(x_1) = 5 != 0 and f is not in V_n. Such a g exists over any finite sample set, so the characterization fails for every m. The correct criterion is the one used later in Section 4.2 (f in col(W^{1/2}V) on the samples).

failure_location.quote: Note that $\E[\bm Y|\XX]\in \col(\bm X)$ only if $f-f^*$ vanishes at $x_i$, i.e., $f\in V_n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sentence by the correct criterion: E[Y|X] in col(X) iff f coincides on X with some element of V_n (in particular if f in V_n), and delete the false equivalence with f in V_n.
issues.overall_effect: The exposition misstates when the reweighted (Gauss-Markov) estimator is bias-free, overstating the obstruction; no formal result or proof relies on this claim (Section 4.2 correctly quantifies the bias via z_2), so the effect is confined to the motivational discussion.
issues.title: False 'only if' characterization of when E[Y|X] lies in the column space of the design (Section 2)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a false expository claim; no theorem, proof, rate, or advertised scope depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $R^\top_i$ denote the $i$th row vector of $\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V$.
\bm U(\bm p) \coloneq \bm V^\top\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm\Sigma(\bm p)^{-1}\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V.
Proceeding with such operations until $|\supp_{\delta}(\bm q_n^{*})|\leq n(n+1)/2$ finishes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: From the definitions of U(p) and Sigma(p) one gets U(p) = L sum_i (p_i/sigma_i^2) v(x_i)v(x_i)^T, while R_i R_i^T (rows of W^{1/2}V) equals (w_i/m) v(x_i)v(x_i)^T. A perturbation q* + t a therefore preserves U, and hence optimality of H, only if sum_i (a_i/sigma_i^2) v(x_i)v(x_i)^T = 0, i.e. sum_i (m a_i/(w_i sigma_i^2)) R_i R_i^T = 0. The displayed condition sum_i (a_i/sigma_i^2) R_i R_i^T = 0 is a different condition (correct only when w is constant on the support), so the claimed invariance of the objective along a fails in general under Christoffel sampling. Moreover, q* + t a remains in the simplex only if sum_i a_i = 0; kernel directions with sum_i a_i != 0 require a separate normalization/homogeneity argument showing they contradict optimality (otherwise the dimension count yields only n(n+1)/2 + 1), and this nontrivial step is missing.

failure_location.quote: there exists a direction $\bm a = (a_1, \ldots, a_m)^\top$ supported on $\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ such that  $\sum_{i\in [m]}\frac{a_i}{\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR^\top_i = 0$. Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the invariance condition with the correct weighting (equivalently, let R_i be the rows of V rather than of W^{1/2}V), and complete the perturbation argument: show that kernel directions with sum_i a_i != 0 contradict optimality via q~(t) = (q* + t a)/(1 + t sum a_i) together with the homogeneity H(q~(t)) = (1 + t sum a_i) H(q*), after which only directions with sum_i a_i = 0 remain and the support reduction terminates at |supp_delta(q*)| <= n(n+1)/2.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the support bound (eq. spt) in Lemma mkjh is invalid as written. The bound itself is a classical A-optimal design fact and its only downstream use is interpretive (a fixed number of evaluation points as m grows), so no other result is invalidated.
issues.title: Wrong invariance condition and missing simplex-feasibility step in the sparsity proof of Lemma mkjh
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement is true and classical; the repair is a short standard argument internal to the existing proof, with no new lemma, construction, reoptimization, or downstream loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The boosting step needs an integer l with l*k <= n and 2^l >= 1/delta, i.e. l >= log_2(1/delta) = log(1/delta)/log 2 with 1/log 2 approximately 1.443. The hypothesis only gives n/k > 1.5 log(1/delta); the slack 1.5 - 1.443 cannot absorb the integrality gap, so for admissible parameters the required blocks do not fit: e.g. delta = e^{-7}, k = 100, n = 1051 satisfies n > 1.5 log(1/delta) k = 1050, but only floor(1051/100) = 10 < 11 = ceil(log_2(1/delta)) blocks fit, so the final inference fails (the proof's own note 2/log 2 < 3 indicates a constant 3, not 1.5). Moreover, for delta > e^{-2/3} the hypothesis does not even force n >= k, and there the conclusion is false: e.g. delta = 0.9, k = 100, n = 16 (admissible since 16 > 1.5 log(1/0.9) 100 = 15.8), with f nonzero and g = f + sigma_0*xii where xii is an i.i.d. +/-1 field on a large finite Omega; the best approximation from 16 such random functions is of order sigma_0/sqrt(16) = 0.25 sigma_0 with probability approaching 1, while epsilon = sqrt(2/k) sigma_0 = 0.141 sigma_0, so the claimed success event has probability tending to 0, below 1 - delta = 0.1.

failure_location.quote: Choosing $l\geq \log(1/\delta)/\log 2$ and noting $2/\log 2<3$ yields the desired result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to n >= k*ceil(log_2(1/delta)) (e.g. replace the constant 1.5 by 3 for delta <= 1/2 and additionally require n >= k), leaving the conclusion unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:rb's guarantee is unsupported for some admissible parameters at essentially all delta > e^{-17} (integrality gaps) and is false for delta > e^{-2/3} with n < k. Its uses (baseline approximation-capacity result for the random subspaces, cited in the contributions and the numerical discussion) survive once the hypothesis is strengthened; Theorem thm:984 is independent and unaffected.
issues.title: Hypothesis n > 1.5 log(1/delta) k in Theorem thm:rb is insufficient for its boosting proof, and the theorem is false for delta near 1
issues.why_classification: The failure is repaired by a standard local strengthening of the hypothesis (a constant change plus an n >= k condition); the method, conclusion, rate n ~ k log(1/delta), and advertised scope all survive.
